{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOVQjqe88AAAABZQYz5A", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4Bn3INzhC3edo", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4Bn3IN", "number": 53, "title": "Implement living terminal-only OLT chat rooms with shared resident identities and natural arrivals", "body": "## Problem

The original PC-VAN had OLT (On-Line Talk), a simultaneous chat experience distinct from asynchronous SIG forum posts. The current reconstructed DAISIZEN `OLT` entry is only an empty collection view showing `参加者：0人`; there are no enter/speak/leave commands, local transcript, changing attendance, or recognizable regulars. The user wants to join an evening room, find familiar SIG/mail correspondents there, converse in the terminal, and watch people arrive or leave as their daily routine allows.

A persistent browser tab is not a real multiplayer server. Recreate a plausible **local simulated room** responsibly, keeping its interaction distinct from forums and mail while never claiming remote people are connected.

## Expected outcome

- Provide a functional OLT room directory and enter/leave experience from the existing SIG `OLT` route, operated **entirely through the PC-VAN terminal input**. In a room, the user sees a compact attendance list, dated/speaker-attributed chat lines and text prompts; can speak by typing, read a bounded room transcript, see arrivals/departures, list users, leave with an unambiguous command and safely re-enter.
- **Realistic but bounded presence:** the existing ten stable fictional resident identities (same IDs and handles used in SIGs and the planned mail #52) visit rooms at suitable hours, may listen silently, greet another participant, chat, depart or be absent. They need not all appear or always answer. An evening visit should sometimes encounter a few residents, with occasional empty rooms too. Repeated room entries or refreshes must not artificially duplicate entrances, lines or participants.
- A visitor can speak naturally to a room and may receive a later response from an interested, present resident after a plausible short delay when an already authorized local AI model is available. OLT turns should flow **more quickly than forum replies** while remaining paced and interruption-safe. Two residents can also converse. **No GENERATE/PREVIEW/SEND or manual AI approval.**
- The local user's established human handle is reused; optional first-run handle registration remains terminal-native. Shared cross-service context/affinities may carry over from SIG conversations and mail when appropriate, but OLT must not fabricate a received private mail or leak the contents of another correspondent's private conversation into a public chat.
- Keep the real application setup (AI model download/consent, profile/presence options, backup/reset, provenance) in `設定 / Options`, **not** as intrusive simulated OLT UI. No model or WebGPU means terminal navigation/readback still works, and no invented model-generated replies or fabricated remote participants appear as if AI generated them.
- Separate **documented historical evidence** from reconstructed interaction controls. The DAISIZEN memorial and operator guide establish OLT's existence/description, and a circa-1996 client listing mentions OLT support; they do not establish period-accurate join/say/leave syntax or screen layout. Research before implementing and label invented UX as reconstructed in Settings/research docs, without normal-screen immersion-breaking commentary.

## Context

Current `main` at filing: `a5e766adf1606b93242d241d823605f471b34d20`; recheck before coding. Existing code: `src/navigation.ts` → DAISIZEN service `OLT`, `src/sections.ts` maps `OLT` to `room` with empty-state text. `src/storage/schema.ts` has no OLT transcript/presence records. `src/ai/personas.ts`, `src/ai/activity.ts`, `src/ai/controls.ts` and `src/ai/activity-runner.ts` provide resident routines, a local consent boundary, shared model worker and bounded generation. `src/terminal.ts`/`src/commands.ts` handle single-input text and IME; OLT must not interfere with `WRITE` drafts or other active command flows.

Historical references: [existing evidence notes](https://github.com/takahirox/pcvan/blob/main/docs/research/pcvan-1996-1997.md), [DAISIZEN memorial archive](https://www.chayagate.com/daisizen/index.htm), [1995 participation guide](https://www.chayagate.com/daisizen/sig_list.htm), [Vector listing for a Windows 3.1 CROCUS communications script](https://www.vector.co.jp/soft/win31/net/se014206.html). Avoid borrowing ECOM guidance-list commands for chat.

Related work: SIG breadth/culture #51; in-world mail #52. Reuse the existing stable identity and character data; design OLT room/presence storage and migrations to coexist with these services regardless of merge order, rather than requiring a backend or real multi-user chat.

### Behavioral boundaries

Only a **currently open, visible tab** can execute actual AI model inference. The room may display a conservative persisted chronology upon return, but should not simulate uninterrupted realtime inference or invent an enormous session transcript while closed. Use small per-interval work caps, rate limits, idle/silence probabilities and coherent joining/departure times. When a user is typing Japanese or composing another message, background chat output must not alter their input, steal focus or cause their partial message to be sent.

A participant being online in a **local simulation** is not an assertion that a real remote user or another browser has joined. Same-tab and two-tab state must agree sufficiently to prevent duplicate simulated AI turns. Room activity needs a budget independent of or clearly integrated with the existing conservative forum/mail generation budget: do not exhaust the entire forum activity allowance just by observing an OLT room for a few minutes.

## Pre-merge acceptance

- [ ] The existing OLT route opens a navigable room directory or room with useful terminal commands for LIST/WHO/JOIN or equivalent context-scoped selectors, typed room messages, recent room transcript and LEAVE/BACK/MAIN; no clickable chat bubbles, browser compose modal, helper buttons or intrusive model-setup popup are required.
- [ ] Shared user and AI member IDs/handles are consistent with forum users and #51/#52, including after handle selection/renaming and restore; room messages use ordered stable IDs, source/provenance tags, timestamps and author references. Do not invent remote users or silently insert AI chatter without an authorized model; optional pre-authored ambient room history, if included, must be marked as authored fiction and not imply ongoing live AI generation.
- [ ] Resident arrivals/idle periods/departures depend plausibly on individual schedule, room interest and room activity. Empty/quiet rooms are legitimate, but typical evening sessions with model consent sometimes yield interactive conversation. A user statement can trigger a delayed AI conversational turn without a separate generation action; multiple regulars can react or talk to one another, subject to caps and coherence.
- [ ] The active room experience works with Japanese IME, Enter to send, a distinct escape/leave command, history and scrollback. No accidental MAIN/BACK navigation when they are intended as literal chat text unless explicitly using command syntax; conversely user must never be trapped in chat. Explicit HELP and clear context prompts are available.
- [ ] Persist room history and active/presence state sensibly in IndexedDB and JSON backup/restore; reset clears and seeds only the documented baseline. Migration from prior worlds and future SIG/mail records is backward compatible, atomic or equivalently failure-safe and multi-tab safe. Bounded retention/pruning avoids unbounded disk use and duplicated AI utterances.
- [ ] Local AI permission and model setup remain the existing explicit opt-in in application Settings; opening/joining OLT alone does not download large weights. Failed/no WebGPU/offline inference does not freeze the room or fabricate replies. Background model work, cross-tab locking, cancellation and generation timeouts are handled; no duplicate generation across tabs or corruption after import/reset.
- [ ] Historical uncertainty about 1996/1997 OLT join/speak/leave commands and screen format is documented with sources, with reconstructed operation never presented as a proven authentic transcript. Normal terminal chat remains period-feeling and avoids AI technology commentary.
- [ ] Add deterministic fake-time/mocked-model Playwright and repository checks covering enter/speak/who/leave, room transitions, AI participant arrival/quiet/speech/departure, human-to-AI and AI-to-AI exchanges, multi-tab arbitration, reload/catch-up, fallback without WebGPU/consent, user input focus and IME, backup/import/reset, and compatibility with existing forum navigation/posting. Run `npm test` / `npm run build` and report actual results.
- [ ] Update README, local AI service behavior docs, SIG/OLT historical evidence notes and JSON persistence contract. Preserve application Settings-dialog vs in-world terminal-only split.

## Optional validation

A manual 1996-inspired late-evening session with a compatible real WebGPU model can assess talk pacing, persona consistency and absence of repetitive greetings. Physical Japanese IME/mobile keyboard and source research into original OLT controls are useful optional checks, not mandatory blockers.

## Required post-merge verification

None required. Browser tests with fake time, local IndexedDB and a mocked WebLLM adapter cover the implementation before merging; deployment follows the existing Pages workflow.
